{
  "subtype": "exploratory_data_analysis",
  "focus_variable": "state_declined",
  "per_column": [
    {
      "name": "expense_category_type",
      "role": "predictor",
      "is_predictor": true,
      "is_interpretable_segmentation": true,
      "rationale": "Cleanly separated, interpretable expense-type categories (hardware, travel, software) that can be segmented and compared against decline rates and crossed with department."
    },
    {
      "name": "asset_subcategory",
      "role": "predictor",
      "is_predictor": true,
      "is_interpretable_segmentation": true,
      "rationale": "Finer but still human-readable asset categories with well-populated buckets, enabling meaningful comparison of decline propensity across item types."
    },
    {
      "name": "asset_brand",
      "role": "predictor",
      "is_predictor": true,
      "is_interpretable_segmentation": true,
      "rationale": "Interpretable vendor/brand segmentation with reasonable spread; decline patterns by brand are an informative exploratory angle."
    },
    {
      "name": "entry_generation_method",
      "role": "predictor",
      "is_predictor": true,
      "is_interpretable_segmentation": true,
      "rationale": "Manual vs auto-generated is a clear, well-balanced binary that plausibly relates to declines (data-quality/process angle) and can be grouped on."
    },
    {
      "name": "has_source_id",
      "role": "predictor",
      "is_predictor": true,
      "is_interpretable_segmentation": true,
      "rationale": "Presence/absence of source id is a well-separated binary provenance flag that can be compared against decline rates."
    },
    {
      "name": "ci_identifier_quality",
      "role": "predictor",
      "is_predictor": true,
      "is_interpretable_segmentation": true,
      "rationale": "Interpretable data-quality tiers (standard name vs placeholder vs opaque id) with balanced buckets; a natural correlate of declines."
    },
    {
      "name": "is_premium_or_high_end",
      "role": "predictor",
      "is_predictor": true,
      "is_interpretable_segmentation": true,
      "rationale": "Interpretable cost-tier flag; imbalanced (445/55) but still large enough to compare decline rates for premium vs standard items."
    },
    {
      "name": "is_new_procurement",
      "role": "predictor",
      "is_predictor": true,
      "is_interpretable_segmentation": true,
      "rationale": "Interpretable procurement-context flag; identical 445/55 split to is_premium suggests possible redundancy, but conceptually a distinct segmentation."
    },
    {
      "name": "travel_context_flag",
      "role": "predictor",
      "is_predictor": true,
      "is_interpretable_segmentation": true,
      "rationale": "Clear travel-vs-non-travel binary that segments expenses and can be compared against declines; partially overlaps expense_category_type but adds a usable axis."
    }
  ],
  "n_predictors": 9,
  "relationship_informativeness": 0.82,
  "rationale": "The set provides a strong, coherent collection of external, interpretable segmentation variables around declines: expense type, asset subcategory, brand, provenance/data-quality flags, cost tier, and travel context. Categories are well-separated and human-readable, and none merely restate state_declined. Combined with the existing department column, they directly support exploring what gets declined and how it differs by department. Minor deductions: is_premium_or_high_end and is_new_procurement share an identical 445/55 split hinting at redundancy, and travel_context_flag overlaps with expense_category_type, so the effective number of independent informative axes is somewhat less than nine."
}
